observations: Photo 0: A white cab truck with an orange/steel borehole drilling rig mounted on the back; visible mast/frames and hydraulic-looking lines.
Photo 0: The truck front grille and bumper are visible; the rig appears heavy-duty with multiple structural members.
Photo 1: Side view shows the rig structure, hoses/cables, and a large mounted drilling assembly; truck has a worn/dirty exterior consistent with field use.
Photo 1: No clear readable brand/model plate for the drilling rig or the truck is visible in the provided image.
Photo 2: Rear/front view of the truck with the rig; again no clearly readable drilling rig model/serial plate.
Photo 2: The rig mast/boom and hydraulic components are visible, but there is no close-up of key parts (pump, gearbox, drill head) or any working operation.

identity.kind: borehole drilling machine on a truck (drilling rig mounted on a vehicle)

claims.claim: Very sound and working fine borehole drilling machine
claims.evidence: Photos show the rig mounted on a truck, but no running/operating footage, no test results, and no close-ups of critical working components.
No service records, invoices, or date-stamped parts are shown in the photos.
Photos do not show a full inventory/parts list or close-ups to confirm completeness of the drilling system (drill head, rods, pump, electrical/hydraulic components).
No manufacturer name/plate/serial number is readable on the rig or major components in the provided photos.

risks.risk: Whether the drilling rig actually works under load (hydraulics, rotation, pump performance) vs. only being visually intact
risks.proof: Short video of a full start-up and drilling cycle (or at least mast raise/lower + drill head rotation + water/flush flow) with engine running and rig operating.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: needs inspection/repair before use).

risks.risk: Missing or worn critical components (drill head, rods, bits, pump, gearbox, hoses) not visible from these angles
risks.proof: Close-up photos of: drill head/bit area, pump unit, gearbox/drive, hydraulic manifold, and any serial/plate labels; plus a photo of all included accessories laid out.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown completeness (worst case: some parts missing or worn).

risks.risk: Truck condition (engine/transmission/clutch, brakes, tyres) affecting total value even if the rig is fine
risks.proof: Photos of dashboard/odometer, engine bay, brake area, tyre tread close-ups, and a short drive video (or mechanic inspection report).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as truck condition unknown (worst case: truck may require maintenance).

risks.risk: Rig compatibility and capacity (depth/diameter capability) unknown without model/spec plate
risks.proof: Readable spec plate/model number on the rig and/or truck-mounted system; plus any brochure/spec sheet showing drilling depth and bore diameter.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lowest/most conservative capability assumption due to unknown specs.

risks.risk: Potential mismatch/repairs (non-original parts, poor welds, leaks) not detectable from wide shots
risks.proof: Close-up inspection photos of welds/joints and hydraulic lines for leaks; include undercarriage/under-mast views.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may require refurbishment (worst case: leaks/repairs needed).

proof_requests: Video of the rig operating: start-up, mast movement, drill head rotation/drive, and water/flush flow (if applicable).
Close-up photos of the drilling rig’s model/serial plate(s) and key components (drill head/bit, pump, gearbox/drive, hydraulic manifold).
Service proof: dealer invoice/service receipt with date and parts replaced.
Truck proof: odometer reading photo, engine bay photo, tyre tread close-ups, and a short drive video.
response.reason: The photos confirm a borehole drilling rig mounted on a truck, but they do not provide readable model/spec information or any proof of working operation. Without that, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set confidently.
